label: early original-phase q/y/k/2/u/w after a leading x/t/z/j/m
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.6% of activation mass), at early positions t=2..5 (about 93% of mass, peaking at t=3), never at t=0/1, and practically never at the delimiter or in the copy phase. It acts like a conjunction of two token sets: the current input is in {q,y,k,2,u,w} (about 4-5x lift each; 82% of mass), and the sequence begins with one of {x,t,z,j,m} (first_tok x gives 5.3x lift; prev2 x/t gives about 5x). The strongest examples look like x t _ [y] or x x n [q]. It is mostly the first occurrence of the input token (95% of mass). Input token alone gives recall 0.75 but precision 0.11. Adding the early-position and leading-token conditions raises precision to about 0.32 with mass recall about 0.61 (dev). The rest of the activation is spread over weaker token combinations (e.g. o n [k], s e [w]). It looks like a hashed code of the early prefix rather than one clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: y, 2, q, k; t=3: q, k, y, 2; t=4: q, k, y, 2) and the first original token (most: x, z, m, t, j, s; least: e, w, d, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, L=4 & t=5, t=2.
